benchmark_guard.note: Session grid (data/index-history.json) capped at the OHLC archive's latest session; rows after it are recorded here, never used.

method.window: Calendar days. For a timeframe of N days the base is the last close on or before (latest session - N days) and the end is the latest session's close.
method.sector_return_pct: The sector index's return over the window. Sector indices are derived equal-weight chained composites of constituent stocks (data/sector-indices.json keystone, extended in-memory from the OHLC archive between the keystone's weekly appends) — not official NEPSE sub-indices.
method.breadth: positive_stock_count / negative_stock_count count the sector's constituents whose own close-to-close return over the same window is above / below zero; an unchanged stock counts in neither. priced_count counts constituents with a close on or before both window ends.
method.contributors: The three constituent stocks with the largest gains and the three with the largest falls over the window, by their own returns (not weighted contributions).
method.rank_change_1w: Rank on the same timeframe's board computed 7 calendar days earlier, minus today's rank. Positive means the sector climbed.
method.persistence: Measured on weekly snapshots of the trailing 3 years of our derived indices: how often the #1 sector was still in the top 3 four weeks later, and the mean Spearman rank correlation between boards 4 weeks apart. Descriptive statistics of the past, not forecasts.
method.stocks: Every priced constituent per sector, with its own return over each of the five windows (null where the stock has no close on or before both window ends). The stocks panel reads this block; per-window counts reconcile to each board row's priced_count.
method.forward: Live success tracking, separate from the 3-year persistence statistics: each published board's per-window leader and top-3 are recorded, and 20 sessions later the leader's forward composite return and whether it is still top-3 are resolved. Never backfilled; the launch board is the live 2026-10-16 board.
method.benchmark_guard: The session grid is capped at the archive's latest session; any index-history rows after it (e.g. the spurious 2026-10-19 holiday stub) are listed in benchmark_guard and never used for the 1-week-ago board or weekly snapshots.

notes: Sector rows are derived equal-weight composites of constituent stocks, not official NEPSE sub-indices; sector membership is today's map applied historically (survivorship caveat).

Our taxonomy has 11 sectors: Trading companies are folded into Others, and mutual funds are an instrument type, not a sector index. The reference board this feature is modelled on carries 13 rows (Trading and Mutual Fund broken out) and different membership inside shared sectors, so levels differ while rankings track closely at short windows (rank correlation vs the reference's 2026-10-16 board: 0.99 at 7 days, 0.94 at 30, 0.90 at 90, 0.54 at 180, 0.86 at 365 — chained composites with different membership accumulate different long paths).
Price rotation is a relative map of where returns have concentrated — it is not a buy or sell signal, and a sector can top a window while falling less than the rest.
